epithet.en: Daughter of the banished Duke, disguised as Ganymede

1.modern-en: At court with Celia, grieving her banished father. Watches Orlando defeat the court wrestler and falls in love with him. Gives Orlando a chain from her neck.

2.modern-en: Banished by Duke Frederick, who suddenly decides she is a threat. Celia insists on going with her. Rosalind plans to disguise herself as a young man named Ganymede; Celia will pose as his sister Aliena.

5.modern-en: Arrives in the Forest of Arden, exhausted. She, Celia, and Touchstone find shelter. They buy a cottage and a flock of sheep from a local shepherd.

9.modern-en: Discovers Orlando's love poems pinned to trees. Celia reveals that the poet is Orlando. As Ganymede, Rosalind approaches Orlando and offers to cure his lovesickness by role-playing: he must woo Ganymede as if Ganymede were Rosalind.

11.modern-en: Waits impatiently for Orlando, who is late for their meeting. Confides to Celia how deep her love actually runs beneath the disguise.

12.modern-en: Intervenes when Silvius is rejected by Phebe. As Ganymede, she scolds Phebe for her cruelty — but Phebe falls in love with Ganymede instead, complicating everything.

14.modern-en: Orlando is late again. Oliver arrives with a bloody cloth and explains that Orlando saved his life from a lion and was wounded. Rosalind faints at the sight of the blood, nearly breaking her disguise.

17.modern-en: Orchestrates the finale. Promises Orlando he will see the real Rosalind. Promises Phebe that if she refuses Ganymede, she will marry Silvius. Appears as herself, removes the disguise, and all four couples are married. Delivers the epilogue directly to the audience.

1.modern-en: Defeats the Duke's champion wrestler despite his brother Oliver's scheme to have him killed. Meets Rosalind and falls instantly in love. Receives her chain.

4.modern-en: Flees to the Forest of Arden with his old servant Adam, who has been denied his wages by Oliver. Adam gives Orlando his life savings.

7.modern-en: Desperate for food, Orlando bursts in on Duke Senior's forest feast with his sword drawn. The Duke welcomes him graciously. Orlando fetches the starving Adam and joins the Duke's company.

8.modern-en: Sits at Duke Senior's table. Listens to Jaques deliver the 'All the world's a stage' speech. Recognized as the son of Sir Rowland de Boys, an old friend of the Duke's.

9.modern-en: Hangs love poems for Rosalind on every tree in the forest. Meets Ganymede (Rosalind in disguise), who claims to know a cure for love and proposes the wooing game.

14.modern-en: Rescues his brother Oliver from a lioness, is wounded, and sends Oliver to bring the bloody cloth to Ganymede as his excuse for being late.

15.modern-en: Sees the love between Celia and the reformed Oliver and longs for Rosalind herself. Ganymede promises he will see the real Rosalind tomorrow.

17.modern-en: Rosalind reveals her true identity and Orlando receives her from her father's hand. They are married along with the three other couples.

6.modern-en: Reported to have been found weeping over a wounded deer, moralizing on the cruelty of hunters — to the amusement of the other lords.

8.modern-en: Encounters Touchstone in the forest and is delighted by the fool's wit. Delivers the 'All the world's a stage' speech, describing the seven ages of man from infant to senility.

9.modern-en: Meets Orlando and spars with him verbally. Finds Orlando's love poetry ridiculous.

10.modern-en: Observes Touchstone's courtship of Audrey with fascination. Comments on the absurdity of a court fool marrying a goatherd.

17.modern-en: Alone among the characters, he refuses to join the celebration. When Duke Frederick's sudden conversion is announced, Jaques declares he will seek out this repentant duke rather than return to court. He exits the comedy on his own terms.

1.modern-en: Tries to cheer Rosalind. Together they watch the wrestling match. After Orlando wins, Celia is the one who first notices Rosalind's attraction to him.

2.modern-en: When Rosalind is banished, Celia refuses to stay behind. She insists on sharing the exile and helps plan the disguises. Adopts the name Aliena.

9.modern-en: Recognizes Orlando in the forest and teases Rosalind mercilessly about her reaction. Serves as the audience for Rosalind's love-struck confession.

15.modern-en: Falls in love with Oliver — now reformed after Orlando saved his life — in an abrupt, unexplained coup de foudre. They decide to marry immediately.

5.modern-en: Arrives in the forest with Rosalind and Celia. Complains about country life and contrasts it unfavorably with the court, while also mocking courtly pretensions.

8.modern-en: Encounters Jaques, who is delighted by his wit. Touchstone delivers a satirical riff on the passage of time.

10.modern-en: Courts Audrey, a simple goatherd, with a mixture of affection and condescension. Tries to arrange a quick marriage. Jaques intervenes, insisting on a proper ceremony.

14.modern-en: Encounters the rustic William, who also loves Audrey, and threatens him with elaborate pseudo-legal language until William retreats.

17.modern-en: Married to Audrey in the mass wedding. Delivers a speech on the seven degrees of the lie, parodying courtly honor codes.
